title: Extension of a coherent integral filtration across a split biproduct
statement: For a scheme X, a coherent filtration on F, a coherent module A carrying a nonzero coherent integral-ideal pushforward witness, and an isomorphism G ≅ F ⊞ A, the module G has a coherent integral filtration.

source.place: Tag 01YF, final paragraph of lemma-coherent-filter; successor split-sum construction

proof.text: Unpack the given chain c of length m. Set f to the first biproduct inclusion followed by e.inv. Map each chain arrow along the monomorphism f and append the top subobject with Fin.lastCases, giving a length m+1 chain. Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm proves monotonicity; Subobject.map_bot proves the bottom endpoint, and lastCases gives the top endpoint. This also covers m=0.

Recover coherence of F from its top chain member. Apply coherence closure under short exact extensions to the standard split biproduct short exact sequence, and transport across e to obtain coherence of G. The mapped old members are canonically isomorphic to the original members; the appended top is isomorphic to G. Transport coherence along these isomorphisms.

For each old adjacent pair, Subobject.underlyingIso identifies the two mapped members with their original members. The resulting square commutes by cancellation against the mapped target arrow and Subobject.ofLE_arrow. Use cokernel.mapIso to transport the old quotient witness. Equality transport handles the Fin.lastCases indices without changing the inclusion.

At the final adjacent pair, c(last m)=top identifies the lower member with Subobject.mk f. The upper member is top. Use cokernel.mapIso to identify its quotient with cokernel f, then cokernelCompIsIso and cokernelBiprodInlIso identify this with A. Compose with the supplied integral-ideal pushforward isomorphism and retain all its witnesses.
